[ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended books include:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. "The Devil Wears Prada" by Lauren Weisberger: Shares a behind-the-scenes look at the glamorous world of celebrities.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. "The Royal We" by Heather Cocks and Jessica Morgan: Explores complexities of female relationships and identity against a British royal romance backdrop.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. "The Interestings" by Meg Wolitzer: Follows a group of friends exploring themes of talent, ambition, and long-term relationships.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. "The Mothers" by Brit Bennett: Delves into the lives of three teenagers exploring identity, motherhood, and consequences of choices.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 5. "The Last Romantics" by Tara Conklin: Follows four siblings dealing with love, family secrets, and the power of stories.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 6. "The Age of Light" by Whitney Scharer: Based on the life of Lee Miller, exploring themes of art, identity, and sacrifices for love and career.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 7. "Daisy Jones and The Six" by Taylor Jenkins Reid: A fictional rock band story in the 1970s exploring fame, love, and creativity.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 8. "The Immortalists" by Chloe Benjamin: Follows four siblings told the date of their deaths, exploring family, love, and choices.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 9. "The Address" by Fiona Davis: Set in the Dakota apartment building, exploring lives of residents across timelines.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 10. "The Last Equation of Isaac Severy" by Nova Jacobs: Follows a woman inheriting a mysterious equation, exploring family secrets and search for meaning.  
[PREFERENCE] User is interested in "The Royal We" by Heather Cocks and Jessica Morgan.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] "The Royal We" is described as a delightful, engaging, and thought-provoking novel combining romance, drama, and social commentary.
